task.title: Accept CLI option values beginning with a dash without weakening argument validation
task.description: Turn the RED tests from dispatch 001-T39-tests GREEN by fixing blocker F-013 in apps/cli: Node parseArgs with strict:true rejects any option value starting with '-', so base64url identity_id values beginning with '-' (about one in 64) and dash-leading --text cannot be passed at all. The tests are the contract: make them pass without weakening them.
task.scope: apps/cli production code, primarily apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts. Do not modify apps/relay or packages/**.

acceptance_criteria: F-013 (blocker): every string-valued CLI option accepts a value beginning with '-'. All nine declared string options are covered by the RED suite: --profile, --relay-url, --store-key-env, --out, --from, --to, --text, --message-id, --with. A dash-leading value reaches its intended layer verbatim - for --to that means the trust check (exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED), not the argument parser.
A --text value beginning with '-' is accepted as message content, including a flag-shaped value such as '--profile', and is never reinterpreted as an option.

Argument validation is NOT weakened. These must still fail closed with exit 2 INVALID_ARGUMENTS, and the RED suite already asserts them as passing guards: an unknown flag (bare and with a dash value), a missing value at the end of argv for --text/--with/--profile, a repeated option including a dash-leading repeat, an option not allowed for the given command, an unknown command, and a stray positional.
The `--` separator behaviour pinned by the tests holds: a bare trailing `--` is a no-op with exit 0, and any operand after `--` fails closed with exit 2.
The exit-code contract (0/2/3/4/5), the single-JSON-object-on-stdout rule and redacted stderr diagnostics are unchanged for every other case.
The full apps/cli suite, `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass, with no pre-existing test weakened, skipped or deleted.
constraints: Read /Users/Goodea/goodea/projects/echolet/.metaproject/index.md before any repository action; project root is /Users/Goodea/goodea/projects/echolet.
Load and follow the project task-implementer skill (.metaproject/skills/gdskills/orchestration/task-implementer/SKILL.md).

Do NOT fix this by setting strict:false or by removing validation. The RED suite contains six deliberately passing guard tests precisely so that disabling strict parsing cannot satisfy it - unknown flags, missing values, repeated options and stray positionals must keep failing with exit 2.

Orchestrator finding, verified directly against node:util and offered as a non-binding hint: `parseArgs` with strict:true ACCEPTS the inline form (`--to=-AbC` parses to '-AbC', and `--to=--profile` parses to '--profile'), while still throwing ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION for an unknown flag. So normalizing `--<declared-string-option> <value>` into the inline `--opt=value` form before parsing is a viable minimal fix. Careful: parseArgs raises the SAME ERR_PARSE_ARGS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE for a dash value and for an option with no value at the end of argv, so a normalizer must handle the missing-value case explicitly to preserve exit 2; it must not attach a value to a boolean option (--json, --yes); it must not double-process an option already written in inline form; and it must respect the `--` separator. You own the design - if you find a cleaner approach that satisfies all sixteen tests, take it.
